_readme: A banner is a three-week featured run built around one featured Legendary, two
featured Epics and four spotlighted Rares. It concentrates odds and adds pity and
targeting. It NEVER GATES: §3.2 is explicit that every card on a banner enters the
general Drop pool and the crafting catalogue on its release day, so there is no
such thing as a banner-exclusive card. That is why the pool below is the whole
collection and the featured list is only a rate-up.
WHY THE POOL IS NOT LISTED. Listing a banner's pool would be listing the entire
card set, and every card added afterwards would silently miss it. The pool is
derived from the content index; a banner authors only what it FEATURES.
RERUNS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT PROMISED. §4 requires 'a published rerun calendar on the
banner page' and at least two reruns within 12 months of debut. Each banner
therefore carries its run windows as data, all of them, from the start - a rerun
you can read the date of is the difference between a schedule and a rumour.
checkBannerData() refuses a banner with fewer than three runs, and refuses runs
FIRST-TIME REWARDS. §4.1: the first ×1 pull on each banner is free, and the first
×10 grants that banner's themed card back, once. Both are per banner and persist
across its reruns - a rerun is the same banner, not a new one to be paid for again.

_note: Debut banner. The featured Legendary is Neon Idols' Prime Diva; the two
featured Epics and four spotlighted Rares are all from the same faction, which
is what makes a banner legible as a theme rather than as a list.
banners.name: The Encore That Never Ends
banners.blurb: Aurora has not left the stage since the first upload. Nobody has told her she can.

_note: The second banner runs immediately after the first, so the banner page always
has something live during Season 1 and the two never overlap.
banners.name: The Second Funeral
banners.blurb: Gothic Royalty buried the fandom twice. The second one had better catering.
